evidence: Phaedr. App. 23.5: vōce hospitālī cōnfirmātus restitit
Cic. Fam. 6.6 (Lewis & Short): animum sapientissimī hominis
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to confirm or strengthen courage, to instil courage into one, to encourage, inspirit, animate, embolden”.

terms.grammar: verb phrase; addō, third conjugation; with the dative of the person
evidence: Ter. Haut. 542: nisi mihi quidem addit animum
terms.comment: Lewis & Short s.v. addō: “to give courage, make courageous”; also in the plural, animōs addere.

evidence: Plaut. Asin. 638: Bonō animō es, nē formīdā.
terms.comment: What one says to encourage someone (see cheer up!).

phrases.latin: iterum salūtat īdem ex occultō sonus. vōce hospitālī cōnfirmātus restitit, ut quisquis esset pār officium reciperet
phrases.english: Again the same voice greets him from its hiding place. Encouraged by the friendly voice, he stopped, so that whoever it was should have the courtesy returned.

phrases.latin: Jocōne an sēriō illaec dīcat, nesciō; nisi mihi quidem addit animum, quō lubeat magis.
phrases.english: Whether he says that in jest or in earnest, I don’t know; but he certainly puts heart into me, so that I want it all the more.

sources: Lewis & Short: confirmo · Lewis & Short: addo · Lewis & Short: animus
